title: Two rails or a flat board: which one gets down first? The flat board, 0.91 s against 1.12 s
description:
Two rails or a flat board: which one gets down first? The same solid marble, radius 1 cm (2 cm across; I = k m R^2 with k = 0.4; the mass cancels), rolls without slipping from rest 1.00 m along a 20 degree slope; no air drag, no rolling resistance (chosen); g = 9.807 m/s^2. Top band: two thin rails whose contact lines are 1.6 R = 1.6 cm apart, so the marble touches at the contact radius r = sqrt(R^2 - (0.8 R)^2) = 0.6 R = 6.0 mm and its centre sits 0.4 R = 4.0 mm lower than on a board; rolling without slipping means v = omega r, so a = g sin a / (1 + k R^2 / r^2). Bottom band: a flat board, contact radius R, a = g sin a / (1 + k). Both marbles stop on a stop pad at the foot (no bounce; the stop itself is not modelled). Shown at 1/4 speed, five runs on one clock.

Measured:
- Flat board: a = 2.3959 m/s^2, 1 m in 0.9137 s at 2.1890 m/s; spin 218.9 rad/s = 34.8 turns per second at the bottom, 15.9 turns over the metre; spin share of the energy 0.2857 (28.6 percent); grip needed 0.1040.
- Two rails 1.6 R apart: a = 1.5888 m/s^2, 1 m in 1.1220 s at 1.7826 m/s; spin 297.1 rad/s = 47.3 turns per second, 26.5 turns over the metre; spin share 0.5263 (52.6 percent); grip needed 0.1149.
- Ratios: acceleration 1.5079 = (1 + k / 0.36) / (1 + k), time 1.2280 = its square root; margin 0.2083 s. When the flat marble reaches the foot the rail marble is 0.6632 m down, 33.7 cm short.
- Table, flat against rails: 0.2 s 0.0479 against 0.0318 m; 0.4 s 0.1917 against 0.1271 m; 0.6 s 0.4313 against 0.2860 m; 0.8 s 0.7667 against 0.5084 m.
- Energy per kilogram at the bottom: potential drop g L sin a = 3.3542 J/kg; flat: translation 2.3959 + spin 0.9583; rails: translation 1.5888 + spin 1.7654.
- Other rail gaps: 1.2 R apart (contact radius 0.8 R) 0.9843 s; 1.8 R apart (contact radius 0.436 R) 1.3607 s.
- Other slopes: 10 degrees 1.2823 against 1.5746 s; 30 degrees 0.7557 against 0.9279 s (the ratio 1.2280 the same). A 5 mm or a 20 mm marble on rails 1.6 radii apart: times unchanged; the ratio depends only on the gap in radii.
- A sliding ice cube on the same slope (no spin, no friction), for reference: 0.7722 s.
- Galileo's groove, 8.5 punti wide for a ball of radius 10 punti: contact radius 0.9052 R, acceleration 5.93 percent less than on a flat board (TPT 2024 says 5.75).
- Checks: RK4 at dt = 1e-04 s against the closed forms, 44 checks, 0 failed; a half-step rerun agrees to nine decimals (1.121958036 and 0.913660997 s).

Why: on rails the marble touches at a smaller radius, so for the same speed along the slope it must spin 1.667 times faster. The spin takes more than half of the energy (52.6 percent against 28.6 percent on the board), so less is left for moving down the slope and the rail marble arrives 1.228 times later. The ratio does not depend on the marble's size or on the slope, only on the gap between the rails in marble radii.
